skills.name: design-thinking-ux
skills.description: Master orchestrator for the impact.com UX Design Thinking pipeline. Walks a designer Empathize → Define → Ideate → Prototype → Test: asks intake questions, invokes the phase skills (research, write-spec, tickets, ideate, prototype shells, test-plan), and stops at each human gate. Use when the user says Design Thinking UX, design-thinking-ux, start the pipeline, take me through design thinking, walk me through Empathize to Test, or wants a guided run from research through usability testing.

skills.name: ux-install-all-skills
skills.description: Installs all 29 impact.com UX Design Thinking + UX Research pipeline skills (Empathize through Test, plus Frame research skills) into the current project and globally for Cursor and Claude Code. Use when the user says ux-install-all-skills, install all skills, install the design thinking skills, set up the UX pipeline, get started with Design Thinking UX, or a designer needs the full skill pack before using the framework.

skills.name: ux-research
skills.description: Master UX research orchestrator for impact.com. Routes research requests through intake, the Frame (user-context), personas, planning/builder skills, and the Empathize pack (user-research, research-synthesis, synthesize-research, data-analyze). Use when the user says ux-research, /ux-research, start research, research request, what do we know, triage this study, or wants the full research skill set rather than a single phase skill.

skills.name: ux-research-master
skills.description: One front door for the whole impact.com UX pack. First run installs all 31 skills plus the /ux-* starter prompts and writes the routing rules, so after that a plain-English message gets matched to the right skill on its own. Research-led: it asks what decision this unlocks and what the Frame already says before it asks anyone to run a study. Use when the user says ux-research-master, /ux, install the UX skills, set me up, get started, which skill should I use, or opens a UX or product question without naming a skill.

skills.name: data-analyze
skills.description: Runs ad-hoc PostHog and Pendo analysis for impact.com UX Empathize questions (funnels, drop-offs, trends, polls). Use when designers ask quantitative product questions in Cursor, Claude, or any MCP-enabled harness. Alias: data:analyze.

skills.name: frame-maintenance
skills.description: Staleness check and rebuild plan for the Frame. Re-reads every claim against Dovetail and PostHog, says what to retire, what to refresh, and what to research next, ranked by what a decision currently rests on. Run it quarterly, or when someone asks whether the Frame can still be trusted. Use when the user says frame maintenance, staleness check, what should we retire, is the Frame stale, what should we research next, or rebuild the Frame.

skills.name: pendo-guide-strategy
skills.description: The strategic layer before anyone opens Pendo. Sets audience temperature, writes benefit-first copy, collapses the flow to a single step, and defines the three conversion goals that say whether a guide actually recruited anyone. Built for research recruitment and panel building; the levers work for any in-product guide. Use when someone says build a Pendo guide, our guide engagement is low, recruit partners into a research panel, should this be Pendo or email, or why did this guide underperform.

skills.name: research-intake
skills.description: Research request front door for impact.com UX. Four questions, two checks, one route: is there a decision, do we already know the answer, and if not — MICRO (48 hours), SPRINT (1–2 weeks), or DEEP (4+ weeks), run by research or by the team that asked. Use when someone files or asks for research, or says research request, research intake, triage this, route this study, scope this research, is this micro sprint or deep, or asks UX Research to look into something.

skills.name: research-planner
skills.description: Turns a routed research request into a study that is actually worth running. Applies question hygiene, sets go/no-go thresholds, designs prompts that test the thing rather than the idea, picks a sample and its diversity, builds the study, runs the 3-participant rigor pass before the rest launches, and updates the UX ticket as it goes. Use after research-intake routes a request, or when someone says plan a study, design the research, write the discussion guide, set up the Outset study, or draft a screener.

skills.name: research-synthesis
skills.description: Triangulates impact.com UX signals across PostHog, Pendo, Dovetail, Outset and Freshdesk into confidence-scored themes — including what the sources disagree about, and the gaps between what people say and what they do. Use for Empathize cross-source synthesis, Research Insight Monitor follow-ups, or when 2+ sources may agree. Use when someone says triangulate this, do the sources agree, is this real or keyword noise, or what does the evidence actually say.

skills.name: synthesize-research
skills.description: Affinity-maps a single research corpus (one Dovetail project, interview set, or study export) into themes and insight cards — separating how often something came up from how much it matters, and carrying the evidence that argues against each theme as well as for it. Use for Empathize single-source synthesis — not cross-tool triangulation (use research-synthesis for that). Use when someone says affinity map these notes, theme this study, what came out of these interviews, or turn this corpus into insight cards.

skills.name: user-context
skills.description: What impact.com knows about its users, and how confident it is. Ask a question about any user, surface, workflow, cohort or hypothesis and it sweeps Dovetail, PostHog (including session replay), Outset, Pendo and support tickets, grades what it finds, and names the gaps — then pressure-tests a design or a roadmap call against that evidence. Also records new findings back into the Frame. Use for "what do we know about X", "has this been researched", "is this hypothesis supported", "where are our blindspots", "what does the evidence say about this mock", "which of these should we build first", or to log a finding.

skills.name: user-research
skills.description: The gate brief: deep-dives one finding and says whether the evidence is enough to confirm a problem worth solving, or what is still missing. States the hypothesis, the evidence against it, and what the current evidence cannot tell you. Hands routing to research-intake and study design to research-planner. Use when designing the case for a problem, probing a Research Insight Monitor finding, mapping evidence gaps before Define, or looping Test findings back.

skills.name: anti-sycophancy
skills.description: Challenges weak UX framing and agreeable drafts — flags thin evidence, feature- as-goal, and one-sided marketplace claims. Use in Define (write-spec review), critique of one-pagers, or when the user asks to pressure-test a problem statement.

skills.name: brand-operator-ux-persona
skills.description: Applies impact.com Brand-side UX persona and JTBD lenses (operators, ACMs, marketing directors) when framing problems or reviewing specs. Use in Define write-spec, Ideate critique, or Brand UI questions.

skills.name: creator-affiliate-ux-persona
skills.description: Applies impact.com Partner / creator-affiliate UX persona lenses when framing problems or reviewing specs. Use in Define write-spec, Ideate critique, or Partner-side experience questions.

skills.name: design-system
skills.description: Points Define/Ideate/Prototype work at impact.com UX styleguide and component library constraints. Use when writing specs that mention UI, checking tokens/components, before on-brand Ideate mocks, or Prototype handoff.

skills.name: research-builder
skills.description: Builds the instruments a study needs that are not the Outset study itself: a Pendo in-product guide, a human interview guide, the PostHog dashboard that will measure the outcome, and the audience — who to test with, drawn from real feature usage rather than a guess. Use when someone says build the dashboard, write the interview guide, set up a Pendo survey, who should we test with, find me partners who use this feature, or build the measurement before we run.

skills.name: user-personas
skills.description: Points work at the impact.com user persona set — three partner and three brand personas with jobs-to-be-done, workflow maps and per-claim confidence. Use in Empathize to check what is already known, in Define to frame a problem against a named persona, and in Ideate or Test to decide who a concept must satisfy first.

skills.name: write-spec
skills.description: Turns confirmed Empathize research into an impact.com UX one-pager and linked UX Jira epic (Confluence draft + research context). Use for Define-stage problem framing, write-spec, one-pager, PRD draft, or Problem Definition Generator handoffs after “problem worth solving.”

skills.name: ideate
skills.description: Starts Ideate from framing (one-pager/PRD preferred; epic, tickets, Granola, or notes OK): prompts for fidelity/tool, emits an ideation brief, and seeds wireframe or mock directions. Use for Ideate-stage divergence, solution brainstorming, wireframes, mock variations, or Solution Ideator handoffs.

skills.name: prototype-handoff
skills.description: Packages a chosen Ideate direction into a Prototype handoff pack after ux-critique: decision, mock links, coverage report, open questions, DS notes, and epic/one-pager links. Use when the designer is happy with mocks and ready to leave Ideate for Prototype.

skills.name: ux-critique
skills.description: Checks Ideate mocks and concepts against one-pager, PRD, epic, tickets, and notes — coverage matrix plus solution-quality critique. Use mid-Ideate or before prototype-handoff or Test pre-flight when the designer asks to critique, pressure-test concepts, or confirm framing issues are covered (UX Critique agent).

skills.name: brand-prototype
skills.description: Auto-sets up the impact.com Brand UI prototype shell: clones the public Brand template, installs Node if missing plus npm/Vite deps, starts Vite. Use when the user says brand-prototype, Brand UI shell, or Brand prototype in Cursor / Claude Code / Copilot. In Figma Make or Claude chat, use ux-prototyping (those harnesses run a live preview without this script).

skills.name: partner-prototype
skills.description: Auto-sets up the impact.com Partner UI prototype shell: clones PartnerUI-shell, installs Node if missing plus npm/Vite deps, starts Vite. Use when the user says partner-prototype, Partner UI shell, or Partner prototype in Cursor / Claude Code / Copilot. In Figma Make or Claude chat, use ux-prototyping (those harnesses run a live preview without this script).

skills.name: persona-check
skills.description: Walks a design, flow or piece of copy through a persona as a task — where they hesitate, what they look for and cannot find, what they do instead — before it reaches real participants. A synthetic pre-test, not a verdict. Everything it produces is a hypothesis to test, never a finding. Use when someone says run this past a persona, synthetic user check, pre-test this prototype, how would a Scaling Up creator handle this, or check this before we recruit.

skills.name: ux-prototyping
skills.description: Prototype-phase orchestrator for any harness (Cursor, Claude Code, Claude chat, Figma Make, Copilot/Codex): installs missing Brand/Partner tools when a shell exists, launches a live Brand or Partner preview (localhost, Make preview, or Claude preview), then offers to publish a new GitHub repo on the designer’s account. Use when the user says ux-prototyping, start a prototype, Brand or Partner prototype, localhost, Figma Make prototype, or GitHub Pages.

skills.name: accessibility-review
skills.description: Synthetic accessibility pre-test on a prototype URL or Figma flow before Maze or Outset sessions — flags WCAG blockers, focus, labels, contrast, and keyboard paths. Use in Test stage pre-flight or when the designer asks for a11y review before usability testing.

skills.name: adoption-check
skills.description: Checks what actually happened after something shipped. Reads the baseline from the Frame, re-runs the measure in PostHog, says whether the research held, and writes the outcome back as a claim. Closes the loop from research to decision to result. Use when someone says did it work, check adoption, what happened after we shipped, did the research hold up, or post-launch check.

skills.name: test-loopback
skills.description: Publishes Verified usability-test findings to Confluence and Jira as Empathize input after sessions complete. Use after Outset/Maze when the designer wants findings looped back to research context — not for synthetic pre-test output.

skills.name: test-plan
skills.description: Drafts Outset or Maze usability studies from a prototype plus one-pager success criteria; orchestrates synthetic pre-tests before recruiting. Use in Test stage after Prototype is ready, or when the designer asks for a test plan, study script, or session guide (Test Plan Generator).
